stories.title: US strikes Iranian launchers on Larak Island in first known attack in weeks
stories.summary: US forces struck two Iranian launchers on Iran's Larak island on Sunday, a US official said, the first known American strikes on Iran since late July. "Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) forces were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into Strait of Hormuz," the BBC's US partner CBS News quoted US Central Command spokesman Commander Tim Hawkins as saying. The IRCG said the attack on Sunday killed and wounded several people and vowed "response and punishment". It marks the first known US strike in Iran since President Trump paused a renewed military campaign in late July. Earlier this month, the US military said it had finished clearing all mines from the strait's main shipping lane. Larak Island is just offshore from the key port of Bandar Abbas, and sits right on the Strait of Hormuz. Iran is currently making tanker traffic pass by this island for checking and reportedly forcing vessels to pay $2m (£1.5m) to cross. Hossein Mohebbi, IRGC's spokesman called the attack a "strategic and fatal mistake by the Trump regime" and said that the "enemy will pay the consequences of this miscalculation in both the economic and military fields". Iran's Tasnim news agency, which is affiliated with the IRGC, said earlier that the attack was carried out by drones. Reports indicate that two people were killed and two others injured, it said. US President Donald Trump said last week that all mines had been detonated or removed from the Strait of Hormuz. He said Iran has been warned that any ship or boat deploying new mines will be destroyed.

stories.title: Seven wounded in al-Mughayyir as Israeli forces besiege the village
stories.summary: Seven wounded in al-Mughayyir as Israeli forces besiege the village Seven Palestinians have been wounded in the occupied West Bank village of al-Mughayyir, near Ramallah, most of them by live ammunition, local sources told Al Jazeera. It remains unclear whether the rounds were fired by Israeli forces or Israeli settlers. Residents said that Israeli forces who raided al-Mughayyir after the settler attack have since withdrawn to the village entrance, which locals say is now locked down and besieged.
